1.plans: 1) Round 1: test a price near the profit-maximizing point under a simple assumption that willingness to pay is spread roughly evenly between 0 and 4.51. Under that assumption, profit = (p - 1) * (1 - p/4.51), which peaks at p = (4.51 + 1)/2 ≈ 2.75. Price at 2.75. 2) Record units sold and profit. 3) Round 2: if profit is positive, test 3.25 to see whether higher prices with lower volume do better. If profit is weak, test 2.25. 4) Then refine in steps of about 0.25 around the best observed price, using the platform's estimate of the profit-maximizing price as a guide when it becomes available. 5) Keep prices above 1.0 and below 4.51 at all times.
1.insights: No empirical insights yet. Key structural constraints: margin is 1.0 per unit at cost 1.0, so profit per unit equals price minus 1. The price ceiling of 4.51 means the optimal price lies between 1.0 and 4.51. The 2.75 starting point is a modeling assumption (uniform willingness to pay) and should be validated against actual sales data.
